# Introduction

Last time, we defined the derivative of a function $f(x)$ *at a single point* $x=a$. The value $f'(a)$ measures the instantaneous rate of change of $f(x)$ at $x=a$, which we can see graphically as the slope of the line tangent to the graph of $f(x)$ at that point.

In our first discussion problem, we estimated $f'(a)$ for the function $f(x)=0.5x(x-3)(x-5)$ at the points $x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4,$ and $5$. Each of these estimates gave us one number describing the slope of $f(x)$ at one point. But there is nothing special about these six points: we could estimate the slope of $f(x)$ at *any* point $x=a$ in the same way.

If we can find $f'(a)$ for every value of $a$, then we have a rule that takes each input $x$ and returns the slope of $f(x)$ at that point. In other words, $f'$ is itself a *function*!

## From Points to a Function

The interactive graphs below show this idea in action. On the left is the graph of $f(x)=0.5x(x-3)(x-5)$, with the six points from our previous discussion problem labeled. On the right, the values $(a, f'(a))$ for those six points are plotted as open circles.

Use the slider to move the tangent line along the graph of $f(x)$. Each time the tangent line stops at a new point, the point $(a, f'(a))$ is added to the graph on the right. As you fill in more and more points, watch how the values we found last time are connected into a complete picture of the graph of $f'(x)$.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
f = (x) => 0.5 * x * (x - 3) * (x - 5)
fp = (x) => 1.5 * x * x - 8 * x + 7.5

// Viewing window (shared x-range for both graphs; slider uses the same range)
xMin = -0.5
xMax = 5.5
knownA = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
fCurve = d3.range(xMin, xMax + 1e-9, 0.02).map((x) => ({ x, y: f(x) }))

// Store of traced points. Depends only on the reset button, so it is
// recreated (emptied) on each click and otherwise persists across slider moves.
tracedStore = {
  reset;
  return new Map();
}

// Add the current slider position to the store (keyed to avoid duplicates)
traced = {
  tracedStore.set(a.toFixed(1), { x: a, y: fp(a) });
  return Array.from(tracedStore.values());
}

tangentLine = [xMin, xMax].map((x) => ({ x, y: f(a) + fp(a) * (x - a) }))
```

```{ojs}
})
```

:::

We call this new function the *derivative function*, or simply the *derivative*, of $f(x)$. Its formula comes directly from our definition of the derivative at a point: we just replace the specific point $a$ with a variable input $x$.

:::{#def-deriv-fn}
## The Derivative Function
The *derivative of $f(x)$* is the function
$$f'(x)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}.$$
The domain of $f'(x)$ consists of all values of $x$ for which this limit exists.
:::

## Problem 3 - Derivative Functions Using Limits
Use the definition of the derivative to find $f'(x)$ for each of the following functions:

a. $f(x)=\frac{1}{x+1}$
b. $f(x)=x^3$
c. $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are constants
d. $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$
